{"title":"Ishika's Green Leaf Discovery","gradeSubjectTag":"Class 5 · Science · Why Leaves Are Green","readMinutes":2,"scenes":[{"label":"hook","text":"Ishika was sitting in her grandmother's garden on a sunny afternoon, surrounded by plants of every colour. She picked up a bright green leaf and asked her grandmother, 'Why are all the leaves green? Why not red or yellow like the flowers?'"},{"label":"problem","text":"Her grandmother smiled and said, 'That's a wonderful question. Let me show you something.' She took Ishika inside and explained that leaves need to catch sunlight to make food for the plant, but Ishika didn't understand how the colour green helped with that."},{"label":"mathMoment","text":"Grandmother said, 'Inside every leaf are tiny green parts called chlorophyll. These catch sunlight and use its energy to make food from water and air. The leaf is green because chlorophyll soaks up all the colours of sunlight except green—the green light bounces back to your eyes, so you see green.' Ishika realized that the green colour was actually a sign that the leaf was working hard to feed the plant."},{"label":"wrapUp","text":"The next morning, Ishika went back to the garden and looked at the leaves differently. She understood now that their green colour wasn't just pretty—it showed that chlorophyll inside was busy catching sunlight and making food. She whispered to a leaf, 'Thank you for being green and feeding the plant!'"
}],"visual":null,"equations":[],"tryTogether":{"question":"If you saw a plant with pale yellow leaves instead of green, what might that tell you about whether the chlorophyll is working well?","answer":"Pale yellow leaves suggest the plant has less chlorophyll or it is not working well, so it cannot catch sunlight as effectively."},"parentPrompt":"Next time you're outside, help Ishika look at different leaves and guess which ones have the most active chlorophyll by how bright green they are."}
